extracted.intended_audience: teachers and educators, students of education, and those responsible for training thinking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for teaching and training reflective, disciplined inference: identifying natural resources of thought, common sources of error, and practical pedagogical aims (curiosity, suggestion, orderliness) and constraints (testing inference, balance of suggestions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of directing thought (need for training)
rubrics_metrics.description: Thinking is an operation of drawing inferences and reaching belief indirectly; because it may go wrong as well as right, it "needs safeguarding and training." The greater the importance of thought, the greater the evils when it is ill-exercised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize that thought is central to practical occupations (magistrate, physician, etc.) and that education's task is to secure its best possibilities and prevent errors that arise from unchecked inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and guard against natural and social tendencies to error
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural tendencies (rashness, presumption, selectivity for confirming instances) and social influences (authority, language, imitation, sympathy, suggestion) instigate and confirm wrong habits of thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction must both transform individual tendencies into trained habits and fortify the mind against irrational tendencies in the social environment; teaching should work to 'undermine and destroy the accumulated and self-perpetuating prejudices of long ages.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Known classes/sources of error (Bacon's idols and Locke's types)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classify causes of fallacious belief: Bacon's four 'idols' (tribe, marketplace, cave/den, theater) and Locke's enumerated types (dependence on others, self-interest, circumscribed experience, dogmatic principles, closed minds, predominant passions, authority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these taxonomies to identify common fallacies: e.g., dependence on others (unexamined acceptance), self-interest (passion replacing reason), circumscribed experience (narrow reading/converse), and authority (giving assent to received opinions). Treat them as focal points for corrective instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of natural/social sanctions—need for systematic regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: While the necessities of life and social sanctions discipline inference to a point (the burnt child avoids fire), they do not carry us beyond restricted boundaries; where inference has no immediate practical reaction, natural checks are ineffective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on natural consequences or social pressures to produce correct belief; implement systematic regulation of observation and inference conditions to replace superstition with scientific habits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transform inference into proof by regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proof arises when inference is controlled by regulation of (1) the conditions under which suggestion occurs and (2) the conditions under which credence is yielded to suggestions; 'Every inference shall be a tested inference' or we must discriminate between tested and untested beliefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach methods of inquiry and testing so that students can distinguish beliefs resting on tested evidence from mere assertion, and inculcate habits of inquiry appropriate to different problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formation of habits of discriminating tested beliefs
rubrics_metrics.description: The main office of education is to cultivate deep-seated habits of discriminating tested beliefs from mere assertions, guesses, and opinions and to ingrain methods of inquiry and reasoning appropriate to various problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus curriculum and pedagogy not merely on imparting facts but on building dispositions: a lively, sincere, open-minded preference for properly grounded conclusions and routine methods of testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base training on natural resources (three essential factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Training must 'fall back upon the prior and independent existence of natural powers.' Thinking implies (a) a fund or store of experiences and facts, (b) promptness, flexibility, and fertility of suggestions, and (c) orderliness, consecutiveness, appropriateness in what is suggested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and cultivate these three resources: supply subject-matter (experience/facts), encourage fertile suggestion processes, and teach organization/connection of ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curiosity as primary resource—protect and sustain it
rubrics_metrics.description: Curiosity (wonder) supplies the primary material from which suggestions issue; the teacher's task is to 'keep alive the sacred spark of wonder and to fan the flame that already glows' and to protect it from becoming blase, routine, fossilized by dogma, or dissipated on trivial things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design learning that sustains intellectual curiosity: present problems, variety of contacts, and avoid crushing wonder through routine or irrelevance. Recognize limited scope for kindling curiosity—often the role is preservation and stimulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestion: ease/promptness of ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: One dimension of suggestion is ease or promptness—the readiness with which suggestions follow presentation of objects or events; 'some minds are impervious... others reflect, or give back in varied lights.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not equate slowness with lack of capacity; consider context and subject-matter. Tailor instruction to contexts where a pupil's responsiveness can be engaged (connect geometry to manual training, history to familiar characters).

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestion: range/variety of ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: Another dimension is range or variety—the number of suggestions that occur. Too few suggestions lead to meager, pedantic thought; too many can paralyze action or distract from tracing logical sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for balance: encourage exposure and variety to enrich conclusions, but provide selection and direction to avoid paralysis by overabundance of suggestions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggestion: depth/profundity of response
rubrics_metrics.description: Depth distinguishes superficial from profound thought—the plane on which intellectual response occurs. Depth is less teachable but can be encouraged by compelling contact with significant features of subject-matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow time and conditions for deeper digestion of impressions; avoid pedagogies that reward prompt superficial answers over slow, substantive reflection. Provide problems that force engagement with fundamentals rather than mere verbal connections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of mind: value of slowness and depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Slowness and depth may be connected—the 'slow but sure' person digests impressions and produces deeper thinking; rushing for prompt answers fosters superficial judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit time and leisure in instruction; be wary of penalizing slower students whose mode yields more substantial reasoning. Evaluate thinking by quality, not speed alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orderliness: organize suggestions into connected thought
rubrics_metrics.description: Facts and conclusions do not constitute reflective thought unless suggestions are organized; they 'must be arranged with reference to one another and with reference to the facts on which they depend for proof.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach methods of organization: sequencing, tracing connections, testing relations against evidence. Emphasize logical consecutiveness and appropriateness of suggested relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Thinking is specific—not a general undifferentiated faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Thinking is specific: different subjects suggest their own appropriate meanings and ways of inquiry; 'Any subject... is intellectual... in its power to start and direct significant inquiry and reflection.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid assuming a universal 'thinking' skill transferable across all domains without domain-specific cultivation. Use varied subject-matter to develop thinking in ways tailored to pupils' inclinations and strengths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teacher must appeal to learner initiative and existing habits
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching and learning are correlative; training must appeal to and foster powers already active in learners—the initiative lies with the learner and effective teaching requires insight into existing habits and tendencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnose students' current resources and tailor approaches to ally instruction with their natural modes of thinking; teachers cannot create thought ex nihilo but can direct and cultivate it.
